en: be reduced to; fall into a lower state

examples.en: That company fell into a pile of debt in an instant.

examples.ko: 인기 스타가 한 사건으로 비난의 대상으로 전락했어요.
examples.en: A popular star fell into being a target of blame over one incident.

examples.ko: 이러다 우리 가게가 문 닫기 직전으로 전락할까 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried our shop will fall to the brink of closing.
A place that was once a landmark has turned into a dump.

examples.ko: 노력하지 않으면 실력이 평범한 수준으로 전락하기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If you don't work hard, your skills easily slide down to an ordinary level.
I looked back at why I had fallen.

explain: '전락하다'는 좋던 자리나 상태에서 나쁜 쪽으로 떨어진다는 말이에요. 보통 '~(으)로 전락하다' 형태이고, 안 좋은 평가나 처지가 뒤따라요. 좋아진다는 뜻으로는 쓰지 않고, '떨어지다'보다 훨씬 무겁게 들려요.
explain_en: 전락하다 means falling from a good position or state into a worse one. It is used in the form ~(으)로 전락하다 and is always followed by a bad state. It never means improving, and it sounds much heavier than 떨어지다.

examples.ko: 여러 정파가 모여 새 법안을 논의했어요.
examples.en: Several factions gathered to discuss the new bill.

examples.ko: 이 신문은 어느 한 정파에도 치우치지 않는다고 해요.
examples.en: This newspaper says it doesn't lean toward any single faction.

examples.ko: 정파 간 갈등 때문에 회의가 자꾸 미뤄져요.
examples.en: The meeting keeps being postponed because of conflict between factions.
It is a policy that everyone welcomed regardless of political camp.

examples.ko: 선거를 앞두고 정파들이 서로 비난하고 있어요.
examples.en: Ahead of the election, the factions are criticizing each other.

examples.ko: 그 의원은 자기 정파의 이익만 생각한다는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: That lawmaker is said to think only of his own faction's interests.

explain: '정당'은 공식적인 조직이고, '정파'는 그보다 느슨해서 당 안의 계파나 여러 당을 묶은 세력에도 쓸 수 있어요. '정파를 초월하다', '정파 간 갈등'처럼 정치 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A '정당' (political party) is a formal organization, while '정파' is looser and can refer to a group within a party or a bloc of several parties. It often appears in political news, as in '정파를 초월하다' and '정파 간 갈등'.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 손님이 없으면 존립하기 어려워요.
examples.en: This shop can't survive without customers.

examples.ko: 회사가 존립하려면 먼저 신뢰부터 쌓아야 해요.
examples.en: For a company to survive, it has to build trust first.

examples.ko: 이 작은 극단이 앞으로도 존립할 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Can this small theater company keep existing in the future?
A nation cannot exist without its people.

examples.ko: 학교가 존립하는 이유는 학생이 있기 때문이에요.
examples.en: A school exists because it has students.

examples.ko: 그 단체는 후원금 덕분에 겨우 존립했어요.
examples.en: That organization barely survived thanks to donations.

explain: '살아남다'나 '유지되다'보다 딱딱한 말이라서 회사, 국가, 제도, 단체처럼 조직이 계속 있는 것에 써요. 사람에게는 '살아남다'가 자연스러워요. 뉴스에서는 '존립 위기'처럼 명사로도 나와요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than '살아남다' or '유지되다' and is used for organizations such as companies, countries, systems and groups continuing to exist. For people, '살아남다' sounds more natural. In the news it also appears as a noun, as in '존립 위기'.

examples.ko: 쓰레기 종량제 봉투를 사러 마트에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the mart to buy trash bags for the pay-per-volume system.

examples.ko: 우리 동네는 음식물 쓰레기도 종량제로 버려요.
examples.en: In our neighborhood, food waste is also thrown away under the pay-per-volume system.
We've run out of designated trash bags at home.
After the pay-per-volume system started, the amount of trash went down.
Do the nearby convenience stores sell the designated trash bags too?

examples.ko: 종량제 실시 이후 분리배출을 더 열심히 해요.
examples.en: Since the system started, I sort my recycling more carefully.

explain: 일상에서는 거의 '쓰레기 종량제'나 '종량제 봉투'로 들어요. 버리는 양만큼 돈을 내는 제도라서, 지역에서 정한 봉투를 사서 써야 해요. 봉투 값이 지역마다 달라요.
explain_en: In daily life you mostly hear it as '쓰레기 종량제' or '종량제 봉투'. You pay according to how much you throw away, so you must buy the bags designated by your area. Bag prices differ by region.

examples.en: I hope the war comes to an end soon.
The epidemic will be over within this year.
The long conflict finally came to an end.

examples.ko: 이 문제가 종식되려면 시간이 더 필요해요.
examples.en: For this problem to end, more time is needed.
The news announced that the outbreak is over.
Once the fighting ended, the village became quiet.

explain: 주로 전쟁, 전염병, 갈등처럼 크고 나쁜 일이 완전히 끝날 때 써요. 그래서 '시험이 종식됐다'라고는 하지 않고 '끝났다'라고 해요. 뉴스에서는 '종식을 선언하다'처럼 명사로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Used when something big and bad ends completely, such as war, epidemics or conflict. You wouldn't say '시험이 종식됐다'; you say '끝났다'. News often uses the noun form too, like '종식을 선언하다'.

examples.en: The company upgraded its servers, so it got faster.

examples.ko: 소방서에서 야간 근무 인력을 증강하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The fire station decided to add more night-shift staff.
Our team is going to add more people.
The hospital strengthened its emergency room equipment.

examples.ko: 겨울에 대비해 난방 설비를 증강하고 있어요.
examples.en: We are expanding the heating equipment to prepare for winter.

examples.ko: 인력을 증강하는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a long time to build up staff.

explain: '증강하다'는 목적어로 '인력', '장비', '설비'처럼 힘이 되는 것을 써요. '늘리다'보다 딱딱하고 계획해서 키운다는 느낌이에요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스와 보고서에서 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: '증강하다' takes objects that add strength, such as '인력', '장비', and '설비'. It is stiffer than '늘리다' and suggests planned build-up. It is more common in news and reports than in everyday conversation.

examples.en: The court handed down a prison sentence to that person.
Many people think the prison sentence is too light.

examples.ko: 이 범죄는 최대 오 년의 징역형에 처해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: This crime can be punished with a prison sentence of up to five years.
He got a fine instead of a prison sentence.
A prison sentence sometimes comes with a suspended sentence.
The court ruled on a prison sentence.

explain: '징역 3년'처럼 기간과 함께 말할 때는 '징역'이라고 하고, 벌금을 내는 '벌금형'과 비교해서 말할 때 '징역형'을 써요. 뉴스에서는 '징역형을 선고하다'가 자주 나와요.
explain_en: When giving a length, people say '징역' as in '징역 3년' (three years in prison), and '징역형' is used when contrasting it with '벌금형' (a fine). In the news, '징역형을 선고하다' (to hand down a prison sentence) comes up often.

examples.en: The road is closed off because of an accident.
Spam texts were blocked automatically.

examples.ko: 그 사이트는 우리 학교에서 차단될 거예요.
examples.en: That site will be blocked at our school.

examples.ko: 차단되는 번호는 전화가 와도 울리지 않아요.
examples.en: A blocked number does not ring even when it calls.
The sunlight is blocked, so the room is cool.

examples.ko: 한 번 차단되고 나면 메시지를 보낼 수 없어요.
examples.en: Once you are blocked, you cannot send messages.

explain: '막히다'는 길이나 코처럼 자연스럽게 막힌 상태에도 쓰지만, '차단되다'는 누군가 일부러 못 지나가게 한 경우에 써요. 번호, 사이트, 햇빛, 소음에 자주 써요. 사람이 하면 '차단하다', 막힌 쪽은 '차단되다'예요.
explain_en: '막히다' can describe a naturally blocked road or nose, but '차단되다' is for something deliberately kept from passing. It is common with phone numbers, websites, sunlight and noise. The one who blocks does '차단하다'; the blocked side is '차단되다'.

dis.h: cut off deliberately, like signal or access

p.n: 막히다 is more casual and sounds like something is in the way; 차단되다 means it was cut off.

examples.en: Jobs were created as the new factory opened.

examples.ko: 이 사업으로 큰 이익이 창출될 거예요.
examples.en: This business will generate a big profit.
I learned about the process in which new value is created.
When jobs are created, young people come back to the city.

examples.ko: 기술 덕분에 수백 개의 새 직업이 창출되었어요.
examples.en: Hundreds of new occupations were created thanks to technology.
The revenue that was generated was reused in the region.

explain: '창출되다'는 거의 '일자리, 가치, 수익, 이익'과 함께 쓰는 뉴스와 경제 말이에요. 요리나 물건이 만들어졌다고 할 때는 쓰지 않아요. 능동형은 '창출하다'이고, 신문에서는 '일자리를 창출하다'가 가장 흔해요.
explain_en: '창출되다' is a news and economics word used almost only with things like jobs, value, revenue and profit. You don't use it for a dish or an object being made. The active form is '창출하다', and '일자리를 창출하다' is the most common phrase in newspapers.

p.n: 생성되다 sounds unnatural for jobs; it is used for files, data and natural processes.

examples.en: A scandal about the celebrity came out in the news.

examples.ko: 그 정치인은 추문 때문에 자리에서 물러났어요.
examples.en: That politician stepped down because of a scandal.
The company was caught up in a scandal, and its stock price fell.
I heard they lied to cover up the scandal.
Rumors and scandals spread fast.
The singer whose image suffered from a scandal made a comeback.

explain: 도덕적으로 좋지 않은 일이 소문이나 기사로 알려진 것을 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '스캔들'이라고 많이 하고, '추문'은 기사나 글에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It means a morally embarrassing matter that has become known through rumor or news. In everyday talk people often say '스캔들', while '추문' shows up more in articles and writing.

examples.en: The neighboring country's army crossed the border.
You must not invade other people's privacy.

examples.ko: 동생이 제 방을 침범해서 화가 났어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling barged into my room, and I got angry.

examples.ko: 새로 온 사람이 제 자리를 침범하는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It feels like the newcomer is encroaching on my spot.
Do not infringe on other people's rights.
I demanded an apology from the person who had intruded.

explain: '침입하다'는 건물이나 장소에 몰래 들어가는 쪽이고, '침범하다'는 땅·권리·사생활 같은 남의 영역을 넘어오는 쪽이에요. 도둑은 '침입'하고, 영해와 사생활은 '침범'해요.
explain_en: '침입하다' is about sneaking into a building or place, while '침범하다' is about crossing into someone else's territory, rights, or privacy. A thief '침입하다', but territorial waters and privacy are '침범하다'.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 상장 퇴출 위기에 놓였어요.
examples.en: That company is in danger of being delisted.
The player who broke the rules was kicked out of the tournament.

examples.ko: 안전 기준을 못 지킨 제품은 시장에서 퇴출돼요.
examples.en: Products that fail safety standards are pulled from the market.

examples.ko: 방송에서 논란이 된 출연자의 퇴출을 요구하는 글이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many posts demanding the removal of a controversial guest from the show.

examples.ko: 실적이 나쁜 가게는 퇴출 대상이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: A store with poor results can become a target for removal.

examples.ko: 퇴출 소식에 그 팀 팬들이 크게 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The team's fans were shocked at the news of the expulsion.

explain: 어떤 곳이나 자리에서 쫓겨나 나가게 될 때 써요. 회사의 상장, 시장, 방송, 대회처럼 공식적인 곳에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 학생이 학교에서 나가는 건 '퇴학', 직원이 회사에서 나가는 건 '해고'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when something or someone is forced out of a place or position. It is a stiff word for official settings like stock listings, markets, broadcasts, or tournaments. A student leaving school this way is 퇴학, and an employee is 해고.

en: be biased; be skewed; be inclined toward one side

examples.ko: 이 뉴스는 한쪽 입장으로 편향되어 있어요.
examples.en: This news report is biased toward one side.

examples.ko: 편향된 생각을 버리고 다시 판단해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's drop the biased thinking and judge again.

examples.ko: 설문 결과가 젊은 사람에게 편향돼 있어요.
examples.en: The survey results are skewed toward young people.
People easily become biased by their own experience.

examples.ko: 식사가 고기에 편향되면 건강에 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: If your meals lean too heavily on meat, it is not good for your health.
The article was so biased that it was hard to believe.

explain: 한쪽으로 치우쳐서 공정하지 않은 상태를 말해요. 뉴스, 시각, 생각, 자료와 자주 같이 써요. '치우치다'는 일상에서도 쓰지만 편향되다는 글이나 뉴스 느낌이 나요. 반대로 공평하고 균형 잡힌 것은 '공정하다', '균형이 잡히다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes leaning to one side in a way that is not fair. It often goes with news, viewpoints, thinking, and data. '치우치다' also works in daily talk, while 편향되다 sounds like writing or news. The opposite, being fair and balanced, is '공정하다' or '균형이 잡히다'.

en: bomb; carry out an air raid on

examples.en: During the war, planes bombed the city.

examples.ko: 비행기가 다리를 폭격하는 장면이 영화에 나와요.
examples.en: A scene where a plane bombs a bridge appears in the movie.
There was a plan to bomb the enemy base.
The news reported the fact that the village had been bombed.
The planes carried out a bombing run, and the building collapsed.
They bombed first, and then the soldiers moved in.

explain: 비행기 같은 것으로 위에서 폭탄을 떨어뜨려 공격하는 것에 써요. '폭파하다'는 다리나 건물을 터뜨려 부수는 일이라서 달라요. 전쟁 뉴스나 역사 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is for attacking by dropping bombs from above, with aircraft for example. 폭파하다 is different: it means blowing up a bridge or building. It shows up often in war news and history.

examples.en: I am unhappy with the verdict, so I am preparing an appeal.

examples.ko: 항소는 판결이 나온 뒤 정해진 기간 안에 해야 해요.
examples.en: An appeal has to be filed within a set period after the ruling.
The lawyer explained the grounds for the appeal.

examples.ko: 항소가 받아들여져서 재판을 다시 하게 됐어요.
examples.en: The appeal was accepted, so the trial is being held again.
The company accepted the ruling without an appeal.
New evidence is important in this appeal.

explain: 1심 판결 뒤에 하는 것이 '항소'이고, 2심 뒤에 대법원에 하는 것은 '상고'예요. 보통 '항소를 하다', '항소를 제기하다'로 쓰고, 동사로는 '항소하다'를 써요. 뉴스와 법 이야기에서만 나와요.
explain_en: An appeal made after a first trial is 항소; one made to the Supreme Court after the second trial is 상고. It is used as '항소를 하다' or '항소를 제기하다', and the verb form is 항소하다. It appears only in news and legal talk.

examples.en: The work changed suddenly, so my head is a mess.
Right after the accident, the scene was chaotic.
In chaotic times, act calmly.
The explanation is so complicated that I'm even more confused.

examples.ko: 마음이 혼란하면 일단 쉬는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: When your mind is in turmoil, it's best to rest first.
I'm so confused that I don't know where to start.

explain: 머릿속이 정리되지 않을 때도, 사회나 장소가 질서 없이 뒤죽박죽일 때도 써요. '혼란스럽다'는 그런 느낌이 든다는 말이라 사람 마음에 더 자주 쓰이고, '혼란하다'는 상황·시기·현장에 어울려요. '복잡하다'는 얽혀 있다는 뜻이라 질서가 무너졌다는 느낌은 없어요.
explain_en: Covers both a muddled mind and a society or place without order. '혼란스럽다' is more about how you feel, while '혼란하다' fits situations, periods and scenes. '복잡하다' only means tangled, with no sense that order has collapsed.

examples.en: Fake news is rampant on the internet these days.
Scam texts are everywhere, so we have to be careful.
During exam season, false rumors tend to run wild.
We cleaned up the street where illegal ads were rampant.

examples.ko: 이런 나쁜 습관이 횡행하게 두면 안 돼요.
examples.en: We shouldn't let these bad habits run rampant.
They say cheating was rampant in the past.

explain: 소문, 사기, 부정행위 같은 나쁜 일이 거리낌 없이 널리 퍼질 때 써요. 좋은 일이나 중립적인 일에는 '유행하다'를 써요. 뉴스나 글에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Use it when bad things such as rumors, scams or cheating spread widely without restraint. For good or neutral things, use '유행하다' instead. You often see it in news and writing.
